title: Geo handoff signal leak caused cross-region fanout and variant fallbacks — incident review
creator: Aisha Kumari
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~14:23 UTC a configuration drift allowed region-level 'handoff' markers to be published without proper tombstone TTLs. This caused a rapid multi-region fanout where the control plane considered nodes in Region-B drained when they were not yet fully decommissioned. The routing layer subsequently re-routed traffic to distant regions with higher latency and, under load, began selecting smaller fallback model variants to preserve latency SLOs. The combined effect was increased 95th/99th latency for several tenant routes and bursty token-cost increases for affected customers. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate remediation, and follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 14:23 UTC — Synthetic alert: per-route 99th latency spikes observed in US-West cluster.
2026-03-09 14:26 UTC — Oncall (Liam) triaged; initial hypothesis: regional hardware degradation. Began tracing request paths.
2026-03-09 14:33 UTC — Control-plane event stream shows a burst of 'handoff:drain' events emitted for Region-B by autoscaler process. TTL field missing from tombstone records.
2026-03-09 14:40 UTC — Smart-router started cross-region reroutes to EU-Central and APAC as fallback; latency rose on affected routes.
2026-03-09 14:48 UTC — Fallback policy kicked in: variant selector chose smaller quantized models for some routes, producing increased token counts and reduced quality.
2026-03-09 15:05 UTC — Mitigation: rollback of autoscaler config push that introduced tombstone change and manual purging of stale handoff markers. Traffic rebalanced to original region.
2026-03-09 16:10 UTC — Metrics back within normal bounds; began post-incident data collection and impact accounting.
root_cause: A recent autoscaler change (PR #github.com/redwood/infer/pull/8341) introduced a new tombstone representation for region drains but did not set a TTL. The control plane's tombstone handling assumed TTL-less marks were permanent and propagated handoff signals across the region aggregator. This propagation path lacked a debounce threshold, so transient signals caused broad fanout. The router's fallback policy then applied smaller variants under the perceived capacity constraints, cascading into higher token costs and latency instability.
remediation: Reverted autoscaler PR that introduced the tombstone representation (rolled back 2026-03-09 15:05 UTC).
Added validation in the control-plane API to reject tombstone inserts without explicit TTL or an explicit 'permanent' flag. (PR #github.com/redwood/infer/pull/8367)
Introduced a 2-second debounce window in the region aggregator before broadcasting handoff events to routing (config runtime-1.20 patch).
Updated router variant selector to prefer local capacity and to require sustained capacity signals for >5s before switching to smaller model variants. (safety window).
Runbook update: incident playbook now includes a quick query to list recent tombstone inserts and a one-click rollback link for autoscaler changes.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-99230: Add end-to-end integration test that simulates transient tombstone inserts and asserts no cross-region broadcast within debounce window (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 2026-03-22).
ENG-99231: Dashboard tile to show 'recent tombstones by region' with TTL and origin + alarm when >5 within 1min from same origin (owner: Marco Nguyen, ETA: 2026-03-19).
ENG-99232: Formalize variant-selection safety budget — add unit tests and runtime configuration with per-route overrides (owner: Lina Martins, ETA: 2026-04-01).
ENG-99233: Postmortem review session with Platform and Product to decide SLA communication and customer refunds for impacted tenants (owner: Liam O'Rourke, meeting: 2026-03-16).
